## Why

K2 GX-04 — L2 NEW-11 measured 0 of 9 sampled procurement contracts
concerning surveillance: an unfiltered buyer→seller graph would pull
unrelated city contracts into the surveillance supply chain (K2 NEW-7,
R-5). The relevance rule derives each notice's verdict from
`matched_keyword` and products/CPV/NAICS where present; under the
answered D-K2-5 decision an unclassified notice is excluded from the
surveillance surfaces (never silently dropped) and appears only as a
buyer-page row carrying the H-13 label.

## What lands

- **`policy/src/policy/procurement_relevance.py`** (new) —
  `sig.procurement-relevance/1`, the ONE classification every surface
  reads (the same one-derivation posture as `policy.labels`):
  - `classify_notice` — `surveillance_related` when the notice carries
    a `matched_keyword` claim (the extraction-time verbatim scan's
    match of record — reviewed term ids) or a product/service
    classification value matching the **reviewed** vocabulary;
    `not_classified` otherwise, including a notice with no
    classification claims at all — the typed absence, never a guess.
  - `load_reviewed_vocabulary` — reads the connectors' committed vocab
    tables (`agenda_content_vocab.toml` + `procurement_vocab.toml`)
    **as data** via stdlib `tomllib` (the `exports.jurisdictions`
    posture; `connectors` is not a policy dependency): the verbatim-
    scan term set, the TED sweep keyword patterns, the acquisition-term
    literals, and the verified `ted_eu_sweep.cpv_codes` set. The NAICS
    slot is **declared and empty** — no reviewed NAICS set exists
    today (I8 owns new-source classification); it joins
    `naics_codes` the day a reviewed set lands. The document binds the
    vocabulary by sha256 over the source bytes.
  - Fail-closed posture: a code no reviewed set names, a term the
    vocabulary does not carry, and a subject outside the notice family
    (`procurement_notice:`/`notice:`) all land on `not_classified` —
    "no reviewed signal found", never the claim "not surveillance"
    (K2 NEW-7's honest surface). Product-code matches are exact (a
    hierarchical-prefix guess is a classification the review never
    made); literal scans are word-boundary compiled.
  - `relevance_doc` — the emitted document: schema, publication
    binding, the rule id + the verbatim decision line, vocabulary
    evidence (sources, versions, sha256, counts) and per-notice rows
    (`entity_id`, `subject_key`, `kind`, `relevance`, `bases`,
    `matched`, `buyer_label`).
- **`policy/src/policy/labels.py`** — `procurement_notice:` joins
  `_KIND_PREFIXES` as the K2 "procurement notice" kind (`notice`).
- **`exports/src/exports/spine_export.py`** — a new
  `notice_relevance_facts` export query (every current publishable
  `matched_keyword`/product-classification claim value on the notice
  subject families, keyed through `entity_identifier`) and the
  `web/procurement_relevance.json` artifact — ONE classification over
  every notice-family entity in the label registry (a withheld entity
  emits no row, the label artifact's posture; a publishable notice
  with no claims emits the typed `not_classified` row) — emitted with
  licence, web compartment, schema and `(rows, relevant)` counts on
  the manifest.
- **`web/src/lib/procurement-relevance.ts`** (new) — the TypeScript
  mirror: the row/doc types, `isSurveillanceRelevant` /
  `surveillanceNotices` (the D-K2-5 exclusion filter every
  surveillance surface draws through), `buyerNoticeRows` /
  `noticeRowLabel` (the H-13 buyer-page row — matched technology for
  a relevant notice, the verbatim unclassified label otherwise), the
  `isProcurementRelevanceDoc` fail-closed shape check, and the
  committed fixtures document exercising the rule both ways.
- **`web/src/lib/data.ts`** — `getProcurementRelevance()`: export mode
  reads `<exportDir>/web/procurement_relevance.json` (absent = honest
  empty verdict set — the export pre-dates the artifact); fixtures
  mode serves the committed document.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/test_policy_procurement_relevance.py` (**12**) — the
  closed vocabularies; classification **both ways** (the ticket's AC):
  a keyword hit relevant, a reviewed CPV code relevant (incl. the TED
  check-digit normalisation), a reviewed-literal product name relevant,
  the word-boundary guard; the unclassified notice carries the H-13
  label verbatim; no-claims, unreviewed-code and NAICS-literal notices
  all `not_classified` — fail closed, never a guess; the committed
  vocabulary loads (real CPV set non-empty, NAICS honestly absent).
- `tests/exports/test_procurement_relevance.py` (**10**) — the artifact

  sha256 vocabulary binding; keyword/code verdicts; the unclassified
  notice emits the H-13 buyer label end-to-end; a claim-less

  subjects and `withheld` label states emit nothing.
- `web/tests/unit/procurement-relevance.test.ts` (**11**) — the TS
  mirror over the fixture doc: relevance both ways, the exclusion
  filter, the buyer-row listing and label, the doc shape check, and
